site.title: High-resolution Total Alkalinity
site.description: How a quantile-regression ensemble estimates ocean total alkalinity and its uncertainty.
site.footer: Swiss Data Science Center · Current methods: split-wise near-optimal ensemble · Interactive results identify their source run above.

hero.headline: Estimating total alkalinity, and how sure we are about it
hero.lead: A gradient-boosted quantile model learns total alkalinity (TA) from bottle samples. The current design trains **42 models: 6 data splits × 7 diverse near-optimal trials**, selected from one hyperparameter study per split. Their disagreement measures sensitivity to training data, feature choices and model parameters.

sections.title: Bottle alkalinity, matched to satellite and ocean context
sections.lead: The target is total alkalinity measured on water samples. Each sample is paired with the physical and chemical state of the water at that place and time.

items.title: Total alkalinity (TA)
items.body: In µmol/kg, from the **GLODAPv2.2023** bottle compilation. The linear salinity baseline and boosted residual are fitted to the quality-controlled bottle target.

items.title: 11 candidate features
items.body: Salinity, temperature, nitrate, phosphate, silicate, bottom depth, satellite sea-surface height (ADT), chlorophyll and three unit-sphere coordinates. Each trial may ignore up to two features; salinity and temperature are always retained.

items.title: Use all eligible dates
items.body: The current preprocessing has no fixed 1993 start date. It requires TA, salinity, temperature and nitrate; missing satellite predictors can remain for CatBoost to handle. The earlier run required SSH and covered 1993–2021.

blocks.title: Model inputs
rows: The dominant control on TA; also used as the linear baseline.
Separates water masses that share a salinity.
Biogeochemical tracers; help resolve regional TA–salinity offsets.
Dynamic topography: a proxy for ocean circulation and water-mass structure.
Adds biological context; may be omitted by a trial.
Separates open ocean from shelf and coastal regimes.
Position on a unit sphere, so longitude 179° and −179° are neighbours.

blocks.title: Collocation
blocks.body: Bottle time and position are matched to gridded predictors in the collocation pipeline. Day-of-year sine/cosine is computed during preprocessing but is not selected among the current 11 candidate features. Missing optional predictors are retained; CatBoost handles numeric missing values.

sections.title: From raw bottles to a clean training table
sections.lead: Salinity, quality flags, required values and duplicate records determine which samples enter training. The funnel below belongs to the displayed results run; the earlier run also required SSH.

items.title: Salinity window
items.body: Keep samples with salinity between **20 and 40**. This drops estuarine and freshwater-influenced water, where the TA–salinity relationship differs.

items.title: Quality control
items.body: Keep bottles with WOCE flag **2** (good) whose cruise-level GLODAP adjustment is at most **6 µmol/kg** in magnitude. Cruises needing larger corrections are discarded.

items.title: Complete cases
items.body: Require **TA, salinity, temperature and nitrate**. SSH, chlorophyll, phosphate, silicate and bottom depth are optional at this filtering step.

items.title: De-duplicate
items.body: Drop repeated records of the same cruise, time, position and depth.

items.title: Feature engineering
items.body: Convert latitude and longitude to three unit-sphere coordinates. These replace raw lat/lon in the model.

sections.title: Cruises are never split across train and test
sections.lead: Neighbouring bottles on one cruise are nearly identical, so a random row-wise split would leak information. The data are cut into **7 blocks of whole cruises**, balanced across salinity.

blocks.body: Blocks come from a stratified, cruise-grouped k-fold (salinity quintiles; fixed seed 42). **Block 0 is the test set for every model** and is never trained on. Pick a split below to see which blocks it uses.

items.title: 5 training blocks
items.body: Used to fit the model. Hyperparameters are tuned by **leave-one-block-out** cross-validation inside these 5 blocks.

items.title: 1 validation block
items.body: Different for each of the 6 splits. Excluded from tuning, member selection and refitting. Available for uncertainty calibration; no calibration is currently applied.

items.title: Block 0 · shared test set
items.body: Identical for every member. Gives an honest score for each model and for the ensemble.

sections.title: A linear baseline plus a boosted residual
sections.lead: TA is mostly a straight-line function of salinity. The model captures that first, then lets gradient boosting explain what is left.

items.title: 1 · Linear baseline
items.body: Ordinary least squares on salinity alone (polynomial degree 1) gives a first estimate, `TA₀(S)`.

items.title: 2 · Boosted residual
items.body: CatBoost learns the residual `TA − TA₀` using **MultiQuantile loss**, predicting the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles together. Trials use the candidate features except for their selected omissions.

items.title: 3 · Prediction
items.body: The final output is `TA₀ + residual quantile`: a median estimate plus a lower and upper bound for every sample.

items: TA_q(x) = a + b·salinity + r_q(x)       for q ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 0.9}
loss = mean over q of pinball_q(TA − TA_q)       (CatBoost MultiQuantile)

blocks.title: One Optuna TPE study per split: target 300 completed trials, 50 random start-up trials
rows: None, one or two non-protected features

blocks.title: Inner-CV objective and pruning
blocks.body: A trial is scored by the **median MultiQuantile validation loss over five inner folds**. After each fold, the running median is reported to a 75th-percentile pruner, with 50 start-up trials before pruning. The default is eight concurrent trials per split and two CatBoost threads per trial. SQLite studies resume until the completed-trial target is reached.

blocks.title: How the number of trees is set
blocks.body: Each inner fit trains up to **1000 trees**, with early stopping after 50 rounds. A selected member is refitted on all five training blocks using the **median best iteration count** from its trial’s inner folds, with early stopping disabled.

sections.title: 42 models from data splits and near-optimal alternatives
sections.lead: Each split runs one study. Seven members are selected from its completed trials, then refitted with distinct seeds. This replaces the earlier seven independent searches per split.

items.title: Which data the model saw
items.body: Split k holds block k out for validation and trains on the other five. Members from different splits learn from different subsets of cruises.

items.title: Diverse models with similar loss
items.body: The near-optimal set contains completed trials with loss at most **1.02 × the best loss**. Starting with the best trial, greedily select the candidate furthest from its nearest selected member. Distance equally weights dropped-feature Jaccard distance and mean normalised hyperparameter distance (log-scaled where searched on a log scale).

blocks.title: Selection, fallback and refitting
blocks.body: If fewer than seven trials fall within the 2% tolerance, include them all and fill the remaining places with the next-best completed trials outside it. These fill-ins are explicitly marked in metadata. Trial selection uses inner CV only. Study seed is `100 × split`; refit seed is `100 × split + member index`. Parallel TPE searches are not exactly reproducible from the seed alone.

blocks.title: Members in the displayed results run
blocks.hint: Rows are splits; columns are member indices within a split. Click a cell for its parameters and test scores. Equal column indices across splits do not imply matched trials or features.

blocks.body: The ensemble prediction is the **mean** of the members' quantiles. Because all members share the same test block, every difference between them on that block comes from the two axes above.

blocks.title: Saved run provenance
blocks.body: Training saves the merged configuration, including command-line overrides, as `configs.json` in the run folder. Each split retains its SQLite study and a near-optimal CSV with trial loss, rank and selection flags. Each member records its trial number, dropped features, refit iterations, data fingerprint and validation/test scores.

sections.title: Disagreement between members is a measure of doubt
sections.lead: Member spread and the predicted quantile band provide two uncertainty signals. The current within-split spread reflects selected hyperparameters, feature omissions and refit randomness. The interactive examples below use the displayed results run.

items.title: Member spread
items.body: Standard deviation of the member medians. It measures model disagreement, not a calibrated prediction error.

items.title: Quantile width
items.body: Predicted Q90 − Q10 divided by 2.563. This is a normal-equivalent standard deviation, not an assumption that the predictive distribution is normal.

items.title: Between vs. within splits
items.body: Population member variance = variance of the split means + mean within-split variance. For the current design, the within-split term includes near-optimal model choices and refit randomness. The legacy `hpo_var` field stores this term.

blocks.title: Where does the member variance come from?

blocks.body: On the held-out test block the spread of member medians correlates with the absolute error at **r = {{spread_vs_error.corr_abs_err.member_std|2}}**, versus **r = {{spread_vs_error.corr_abs_err.scaled_iqr|2}}** for the scaled quantile width.

blocks.title: Does the uncertainty predict the error?
Read this as a ranking, not an error bar
blocks.body: Assess both the magnitude and ranking of uncertainty on held-out data. Member spread is not calibrated to prediction error. The plots use held-out predictions from the run identified above.

sections.title: What is still open
sections.lead: Read these diagnostics alongside the source run and its cruise coverage.

blocks.title: Coverage in the displayed results
blocks.body: The displayed run’s nominal 80% interval covers **{{ensemble_scores.all.interval_80pct_coverage|pct}}** of its held-out test samples. Use the source-run notice to identify which method this score evaluates. Quantile averaging alone provides no coverage guarantee.

items.title: Calibrate on validation blocks
items.body: Use validation RMSE to choose between the member std and the scaled Q90 − Q10 as the uncertainty estimate, then rescale it. Compare against the untouched test block.

items.title: Earlier years and missing predictors
items.body: SSH is no longer required for complete-case filtering. Check how much earlier data now enter training and whether missing satellite predictors affect regional accuracy and interval coverage.

items.title: Independent check
items.body: Evaluate on BATS and HOT time series after explicitly checking overlap with training cruises and dates.

items.title: Full-period inference
items.body: Apply the ensemble to the gridded 8-day, 0.25° fields, where the inputs are gridded products rather than bottle measurements.

blocks.body: Evaluation reports all samples and, when bottom depth is available, a subset deeper than 300 m. The depth threshold affects reporting rather than training selection. near-optimal loss tolerance is an empirical model-selection rule, not a confidence level or posterior probability.

explorer.intro: Choose which members to include and click a sample to see how each one predicts it. Only a random subset of {{run.sample_size}} test samples is shown here.

comparison.title: highres-TA run comparison
comparison.hero: Six quantile-ensemble runs of the surface total alkalinity (TA) reconstruction in models/, compared on held-out bottle data, the shared test block, salinity sensitivity, time-series stations and ensemble composition. Errors are predicted minus observed, in µmol kg⁻¹. Data extracted 2026-11-10.
comparison.lineage_intro: The arrows show experimental comparisons, not fine-tuning. Focus, hover or select a run to see its change from the parent.

lineage.title: Independent tuning · 1993–2022
lineage.change: Earlier independent tuning model used only the 1993–2022 GLODAP subset.

lineage.title: Independent tuning · full period
lineage.change: Removed the date restriction and expanded to the full GLODAPv2023 period; the member-selection design stayed per-replicate HPO.

lineage.title: Near-optimal ensemble · GLODAP
lineage.change: Introduced one Optuna study per split and seven diverse near-best trials, with chl_globcolour among the available features. Uses the same GLODAP row set as B.

lineage.title: Near-optimal ensemble · +CARIMED
lineage.change: Added CARIMED Mediterranean bottles to training, changing the block partition and expanding the test set.

lineage.title: Gridded salinity stack
lineage.change: Branch from D: replaced in-situ salinity with the CCI → SODA → multi-observation stack. Config notes confirm the split blocks and test block are shared with the in-situ model.

lineage.title: Stack + salinity predictors
lineage.change: Alternative branch from D: uses the gridded salinity stack and adds sss_cci and salt_soda as separate model features. Compared with E, this also adds standalone predictors; station evaluation is not yet available.

comparison.overview_intro: The two independent tuning runs use the older design (seven separate Optuna studies per split); the four near-optimal runs use one study per split and pick seven diverse near-best trials.
comparison.comparison_warning_title: Read this before comparing headline numbers.
comparison.comparison_warning: The runs do not share one test set. A and B/C use GLODAP only (3,891 and 4,139 test rows); D, E and F add CARIMED Mediterranean bottles, which changes the block partition (4,314 test rows, only 332 shared with C). The Held-out comparison fixes this by scoring every row with members that never trained on it (test block plus out-of-fold validation), so C, D, E and F are compared on identical rows.
comparison.findings_title: What each model gets right and where it breaks

findings.summary: Best headline score, but not comparable
items: strength
Lowest test RMSE of all runs (19.3 all, 16.0 deep) and the smallest member variance (split 11, HPO 5 (µmol kg⁻¹)²).
limit

Trained and tested on a 1993–2022 subset of an earlier data version (3,891 test rows). Its rows cannot be matched to the current data, so the low error says as much about the easier subset as about the model.
limit
Old per-replicate-HPO design; no validation, station or per-member trial outputs.
strength
Same rows as C. Useful as the reference showing what the near-optimal member selection changed.
limit
Slightly worse than C on identical test rows: RMSE 19.7 vs 18.9, CRPS 6.2 vs 6.0, coverage 0.69 vs 0.72.
limit
No validation or station evaluation.

findings.summary: Good in-situ model with a Mediterranean blind spot
items: strength
Best Indian (10.9) and Pacific (13.8) held-out RMSE, and the best RADCOR (Galician coast) station scores.
limit
No Mediterranean training data: DYFAMED RMSE 125 with bias −124; Mediterranean held-out rows bias −79 and 7 % coverage.
limit
Its maps feed it gridded salinity: held-out RMSE rises from 24.9 to 54.9, bias −9, coverage collapses to 0.40, and ≥ 60° bias reaches −28.

findings.summary: Adds CARIMED: fixes the Mediterranean, costs a little elsewhere
items: strength
DYFAMED RMSE falls from 125 to 22 (gridded); Mediterranean held-out bias −79 → −17. On the 28,988 shared GLODAP rows RMSE 23.8 vs 24.9 for C, best in the Atlantic.
limit
CARIMED rows remain the hardest data (RMSE 62, bias −17). Pacific, Indian and 20–40° worsen by 2–3 µmol kg⁻¹; RADCOR station RMSE 12 → 18.
limit
Same gridded-salinity failure as C: RMSE 59.6, coverage 0.42, Arctic/subpolar bias −35.
limit
Headline test RMSE (26.9) is not a regression vs C (18.9): the test block now contains different, harder rows.

findings.summary: Consistent with inference, at a price in accuracy
items: strength

The right comparison for maps: held-out RMSE 44.7 vs 59.6 for D with gridded salinity, bias ≈ 0 instead of −11, and coverage 0.74 instead of 0.42. Station coverage with gridded T/S rises to 0.72–0.83 at HOT, ALOHA and BATS.
limit
Still almost twice the in-situ error (44.7 vs 26.4); intervals are twice as wide (49 vs 25).
limit
Over-predicts where the gridded products miss fresh water: in-situ S < 30 bias +52, Arctic/subpolar +10. RADCOR stations fail (bias +46, coverage ≈ 0), with gridded and in-situ T/S alike.
limit
Split 1 members are much worse (member RMSE 52 vs ≈ 42).
strength
Rows with sss_cci are slightly better than E (RMSE 23.7 vs 24.3). The model leans on salt_soda (15 % importance), not sss_cci (0.7 %).
limit
Overall slightly worse than E: 45.8 vs 44.7 (41.7 vs 40.8 on GLODAP rows); rows without sss_cci 53.4 vs 51.8; 2020+ RMSE 48.5 vs 41.3.
limit
Not yet evaluated at stations (collocation cache lacks the product columns). sss_cci and sss_soda are empty in the store from 2024, so recent maps run on the anchor only.

shared_limitations: Intervals are too narrow. The nominal 80 % q10–q90 interval covers 69–75 % of held-out observations in every run; coastal and Southern Ocean rows of the in-situ models drop to 64–68 %.
Coastal water is 3× harder. Rows with bottom depth < 500 m have RMSE 45–47 (in-situ models) vs 15–20 offshore; with gridded salinity the coastal RMSE is 75–95.
Fresh water and high latitudes. Below salinity 30 the in-situ models reach RMSE 73–78; ≥ 60° is the worst latitude band for every model.
Period effects. 2000–2009 and the 1980s carry the largest errors in all runs; 1985–1994 is the easiest period.

Gridded salinity dominates map error. Moving from in-situ to gridded salinity roughly doubles RMSE for every model, and no feature-engineering change so far (stacked vs multi-product) closes that gap.
comparison.heldout_intro: Every observation is predicted only by members that never saw it: the test block by all 42 members, every other row by the 7 members of the split that held it out for validation (median across members). For the in-situ models the stacked variant swaps in the gridded salinity stack (CCI → SODA → multi-obs), which is what those models see when producing maps. That variant, not the in-situ one, is the fair comparison with E and F.
comparison.heldout_loc_note: Hover or click a bar, a chip or a point to highlight that group. Points are a sample of 6,000 distinct sampling locations.
comparison.map_intro: Held-out residuals binned to 5° cells (cells with ≥ 5 rows). Use the difference view to see where one variant beats another: blue cells mean the chosen variant has lower RMSE than the reference.
comparison.salinity_intro: The validation runner re-predicts each row after replacing salinity with a gridded product, on the same rows. For the in-situ models this measures the error the maps inherit; for E and F the model was trained on the stack, so the stacked bar is its native input and the in-situ bar is the mismatch. Regions follow the validation definitions: coastal means bottom depth < 500 m, and the latitude split is at |lat| = 60°.
comparison.salinity_region_note: Hover or click a region (bar, chip or map point) to highlight it.
comparison.salinity_delta_title: Added error vs size of the salinity mismatch (test block)
comparison.salinity_delta_note: RMSE with the product minus RMSE with in-situ salinity, binned by |S_product − S_reference|. The reference is in-situ salinity for C and D but the stack for E and F, so for E and F the stacked product has no mismatch; pick another product to compare them. A model that is robust to salinity errors stays low on the right.
comparison.stations_intro: Surface bottles from 20 stations, predicted with gridded T/S (what the maps see) and with the in-situ T/S. Station evaluation exists for C, D and E. F has not been evaluated yet: the cached station collocations in data/time_series/ lack the sss_cci and salt_soda columns, so evaluate_stations.py --stage evaluate fails until the stations are re-collocated.
comparison.station_location_note: Click a station on the map or in the table to plot its time series below.
comparison.testblock_intro: Scores from ensemble_test_metrics.json (mean of members). Rows differ between run families, so compare within A, within B/C (identical rows) and within D/E/F (identical rows). Deep keeps rows with bottom depth ≥ 300 m.
comparison.member_note: Each dot is one of the 42 members, coloured by run, grouped by the split that trained it. The ensemble value is the line.
comparison.variance_note: Mean variance across test rows, split into the data-split term and the tuning / near-optimal term (law of total variance), per quantile. Units (µmol kg⁻¹)².
comparison.ensemble_intro: For the near-optimal runs (C–F): CatBoost feature importance of the residual model (mean over members), how often each feature is dropped by the selected members, and the spread of selected hyperparameters. The independent tuning runs did not store per-member trial metadata.
comparison.rashomon_size_note: Trials within 2 % of the best inner-CV loss. A small set means the split had few equally good models to pick diverse members from.
comparison.footer: Sources: models/<run>/ensemble_test_metrics.json, validation/{predictions.parquet, scores.csv, salinity_penalty.csv}, stations/{scores.csv, predictions.parquet}, models/*.json, feature_importance/summary.csv. Held-out predictions use median aggregation (validation.yaml); the test-block table uses the saved mean aggregation. Basins are coarse boxes: Mediterranean 30–46° N, 5.5° W–37° E; Southern Ocean south of 35° S; Arctic/subpolar N north of 60° N; Indian 20–120° E north of 35° S and south of 30° N; Atlantic 70° W–20° E; Pacific otherwise.
